name: Senderz Marketing
author: senderz

sections.description:
Senderz is email, SMS and web-push marketing for online stores and websites. This plugin connects your WordPress site to your Senderz workspace. Once connected it renders your published popups, capture forms and games on the site, and serves the same-origin service worker browser push requires.

It can also turn submissions from the form plugin you already use into Senderz contacts. Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor Pro Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms and Ninja Forms are supported. You pick which forms are captured and which field holds the email address, phone number and name, so no form sends anything until you set it up.

It can sync the people who have an account on your site. Accounts arrive in Senderz as contacts who are not subscribed to anything. Creating an account is not marketing consent, so only a person who ticks the opt-in checkbox you can add to the registration form is ever subscribed.

When WooCommerce is active it sends paid orders to Senderz for revenue reporting, imports the previous two years of paid orders in the background, can add an unticked marketing opt-in checkbox at checkout and attaches the exact pay-for-order recovery link to outgoing order webhooks. Checkout consent fields, identified cart activity and back-in-stock requests are disabled until a site administrator enables them in Senderz.

This plugin replaces Senderz for WooCommerce. Upgrading carries your settings over and deactivates the old plugin automatically.

Your data

The plugin works with the hosted Senderz service and needs a Senderz account. Nothing is sent before you connect your site, and form capture, user sync, cart activity and back-in-stock requests stay off until you turn them on. The External services section lists exactly what is shared.

Privacy Policy: https://senderz.app/privacy

External services

This plugin is a client for Senderz, a hosted service at https://senderz.app. It requires a Senderz account.

Nothing is sent to Senderz until you connect the site. On a fresh install the plugin makes no outbound request of any kind: no storefront script, no tracking beacon, no version ping.

Once you connect, the following leaves your site:

  • Your site address, sent once at connect so Senderz can identify the site.
  • Visitors’ browsers load the Senderz storefront script from api.senderz.app to render your published popups and handle push opt-in.
  • Push subscription details, when a visitor opts in to browser notifications.
  • For each form you switch on under Senderz Marketing, then Forms: only the values in the fields you mapped, the form’s ID, the page address it was submitted from, the list you chose for it, and the visitor’s IP address and browser, kept in Senderz as evidence of their marketing consent. Fields you did not map are never sent. The Senderz lists are loaded from Senderz when you open that screen.
  • With WooCommerce active, the marketing opt-in a shopper ticks at checkout and paid-order details are sent to Senderz. After connection, up to two years of paid orders are imported in the background so revenue reports include existing store history.
  • With WooCommerce active and cart activity switched on under Settings, then Senderz, then Store: when a shopper types their email address at the checkout, that address is sent, and from then on their add to cart, remove from cart and started checkout activity is sent with the product, price and quantity. The address is held in your site’s own WooCommerce session, never in a cookie a third-party script could read.
  • With WooCommerce active, store activity is also counted for shoppers who have not given an email address: the product viewed and, with cart activity switched on, products added to or removed from the cart with their price and quantity, and the cart total when checkout starts. These are sent with a random browser ID rather than a name or address. The storefront script stores that ID in the visitor’s browser and in a first-party cookie named senderz_cid, so your site can send cart and checkout activity under the same ID. For a signed-in account, the account’s email address is sent with this activity so it is attached to the matching Senderz profile. When a consent plugin that supports the WordPress Consent API is active, none of this is tracked until the visitor allows statistics.
  • With WooCommerce active and back-in-stock requests switched on: the email address a shopper enters on an out-of-stock product, and whether they ticked the marketing opt-in, are stored on your site and sent to Senderz when that product comes back in stock.
  • If you switch on user sync under Senderz Marketing, then Users: for each account on the site, its email address, phone number if one is stored, first and last name, site language and whether the person ticked a marketing opt-in. User sync is off until you turn it on.

Form submissions are sent after the page has finished loading for the visitor, so capture never slows a form down. Account changes are sent in the background too.

Terms of Use: https://senderz.app/terms
Privacy Policy: https://senderz.app/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Senderz Marketing in your WordPress administration menu.
  3. Click Connect to Senderz and approve the request in your Senderz workspace.

If your site is not reachable from the internet, for example a staging or local
site, use Manual setup on the same screen with your Workspace ID and an API key
from Senderz under Settings, then API keys.
sections.faq:
How do I keep the plugin up to date?

Open Senderz Marketing in your WordPress admin and choose Turn on automatic updates. WordPress then installs each new version from WordPress.org on its own. You can also turn it on from the Plugins page.

Nothing shows on my site

Check that Senderz Marketing shows Connected, and that you have a published
popup in Senderz. If you connected Senderz with a different site address, for
example www versus non-www, set it under Advanced.

I was using Senderz for WooCommerce

Install this plugin and it takes over automatically. Your settings carry across
and the old plugin is deactivated. Connect from Senderz Marketing so the
site is linked to your workspace directly.

Does this send anything before I connect?

No. Every outbound behaviour is gated on the connection.

How do I capture my contact form?

Go to Senderz Marketing, then Forms. Your forms are listed under the plugin
they belong to. Tick Capture submissions, check that the email, phone and name
fields are pointed at the right columns, and save.

If a form is not listed, submit it once. Some form plugins do not let us read
their forms until one has been used.

Does capturing a form subscribe people to marketing?

Only if you say so. Each form has a marketing consent setting, and it starts at
never. Capture on its own records the contact without subscribing them. Choose
either that the whole form is a marketing opt-in, or that a specific consent
checkbox on the form has to be ticked.

Email and SMS are separate. Point a checkbox at Email marketing consent or SMS
marketing consent and it covers only that channel. For a whole-form opt-in or a
general consent checkbox, tick the channels its wording covers.

Can a form add people to a list?

Yes. Pick a Senderz list for the form and every submission is added to it, which
starts the automations that list triggers. Being on a list is not marketing
consent, so the consent setting still decides what they can be sent.

Does the back-in-stock message reach everyone who asks for it?

No. Senderz only emails people who have opted in to marketing, so the request
form carries an unticked opt-in checkbox. A shopper who leaves it unticked is
still recorded against the product, and you can see the request in Senderz, but
no email is sent to them.

Which WooCommerce checkout does the opt-in checkbox appear on?

Both. On the classic checkout it sits above the order button. On the block checkout it appears under the order notes, and it always starts unticked there because the block checkout has no ticked-by-default option. The block checkout needs WooCommerce 8.9 or newer.
sections.changelog:
2.4.7

  • A clearer settings screen: the plugin logo, version and a connection status badge at the top, the connection details and actions in one card, automatic updates as a single on/off switch, and Manual setup and Advanced folded away until needed. Each section has one button that says what it saves.
  • The Forms, Users and Store tabs stay greyed out until the site is connected.
  • Browsers and password managers no longer fill your WordPress login into the manual Workspace ID and API key fields.
  • The Senderz API address must use https://, so keys are never sent unencrypted.
  • The Forms tab now shows “Do not send” for a field that Senderz or a saved setting does not send, instead of a guess, so both places always show the same field mapping.

2.4.6

  • The marketing opt-in notes on the Accounts and back-in-stock settings no longer refer to one country’s law, since Senderz is used outside Israel too.

2.4.5

  • Faster storefronts: the Senderz script now loads deferred, so it no longer holds up the page, and its address only changes when Senderz ships a new version, so browsers and the CDN can keep it instead of downloading it again every few minutes.
  • The page optimizer opt-outs now sit on the Senderz script tag itself.

2.4.4

  • Form settings now stay the same in WordPress and in Senderz. A form’s list, its capture switch, its field map and its marketing consent can be changed in either place, and the other one shows the change.
  • The Forms tab loads the latest settings from Senderz each time it opens, and the site checks for changes every 15 minutes.
  • Forms set up with the Senderz action in Elementor keep their settings in Elementor.

2.4.3

  • New Automatic updates setting on the Senderz Marketing page, plus a one-time offer to turn it on. Updates still come only from WordPress.org, and nothing changes until you choose it.
  • The plugin now tells Senderz whether automatic updates are on, so Senderz only reminds you to update when it is needed.

2.4.2

  • The plugin now tells Senderz which version it is running, so Senderz can let you know when an update is available. No store or visitor data is added.

2.4.1

  • Changing a form’s list in WordPress or Elementor now updates its list in Senderz before the next lead is captured.
  • Older reports and retried submissions no longer overwrite newer list settings. Page-specific routing and marketing consent are preserved.
  • Choosing the list set in Senderz no longer reuses an older WordPress form mapping.

2.4.0

  • Product views, add to cart and checkout starts are now read from WooCommerce itself, so they are tracked on any theme or page builder, including Elementor and Crocoblock templates, custom templates and translated checkout addresses.
  • These store events are counted even before a shopper signs in or enters an email. When the shopper is identified later, their earlier activity is attached to their profile. Automations still start only for identified shoppers, as before.
  • Tracking respects consent plugins that use the WordPress Consent API: without statistics consent, nothing is tracked.

2.3.4

  • The marketing opt-in checkbox now works on the WooCommerce block checkout. A store that uses its own checkbox there is read too, when that checkbox is a WooCommerce additional checkout field.

2.3.3

  • A historical order or customer sync that stops making progress resumes from where it left off instead of showing “running” forever.

2.3.2

  • SMS marketing consent also approves WhatsApp. The form setting is one choice, SMS / WhatsApp, and the checkout wording names both.

2.3.1

  • A WordPress form can now approve WhatsApp as well as email and SMS. Tick WhatsApp under The consent covers, or map a WhatsApp consent checkbox. Forms saved before this update keep covering email and SMS only until you tick WhatsApp.

2.3.0

  • Senderz now appears in Elementor under Actions After Submit, next to the other marketing services. Adding it to a form turns capture on for that form.
  • The Elementor action has its own settings: which list signups go to, whether the form is a marketing opt-in, and which checkbox the visitor ticks.
  • The Elementor action has a Field Mapping section, like MailChimp: each Senderz field has a dropdown of the form’s fields. Leave it empty and Senderz finds the email, phone and name fields itself.
  • A form carrying the Senderz action is sent once, not twice, and a consent box Elementor ticks by default still does not count as consent.
  • Form fields can be mapped to any contact field in your Senderz account, not only email, phone and name.
  • The page each submission came from is now sent and kept, so you can see where a contact signed up.
  • Your site reports its forms to Senderz, so you can choose each form’s list there, including a different list per page when the same form or popup appears on several pages.

2.2.0

  • Form capture can subscribe email and SMS separately: map an email consent checkbox and an SMS consent checkbox, or choose which channels a single consent covers.
  • Form capture can add contacts to a Senderz list, which starts that list’s automations.
  • Form submissions record the visitor’s own IP address and browser as consent evidence, including on sites behind Cloudflare, instead of the website server’s.
  • A form submission that cannot reach Senderz, or arrives while it is busy, is sent again automatically over the next four hours instead of being lost.
  • Shows one marketing consent checkbox at checkout covering email, SMS and WhatsApp, instead of a separate box per channel.
  • Adds the option to use the checkbox your site already has, set by its field name in Senderz.
  • Adds the option to have the checkbox ticked by default, off unless you turn it on.
  • Shows a notice in the WordPress admin when Senderz stops accepting this site’s API key, with a link to reconnect, instead of failing silently.
  • After a failed settings refresh, waits 15 minutes before trying again instead of retrying on every admin page load.

2.1.6

  • Sends paid WooCommerce orders to Senderz and imports the previous two years so dashboard revenue and order totals match the connected store.

2.1.5

  • Opens Senderz Marketing immediately after activation and returns guided connections to the connected WooCommerce setup in Senderz.

2.1.4

  • First release on the WordPress.org plugin directory.
  • Starts the user sync in the background as soon as it is turned on in Senderz, instead of waiting for the next settings refresh.

2.1.3

  • Verifies a nonce before recording a marketing opt-in from the registration form, the add user screen and the WooCommerce checkout.

2.1.2

  • Renames the plugin to Senderz Marketing and uses the unique senderz-marketing-connect directory slug.
  • Loads the Senderz storefront runtime through the WordPress script enqueue API.
  • Keeps WooCommerce checkout collection and identified cart activity disabled until an administrator enables them.

2.1.1

  • Refreshes the popup runtime after backend releases so storefronts do not keep stale scratch-card and image rendering behavior.

2.1.0

  • Moves the Senderz screen to Marketing on WooCommerce stores, and to its own menu on other sites. The old Settings link still works.
  • Checkout opt-ins, the wording on each, the list subscribers join, cart tracking, back-in-stock and user sync are now set in Senderz. This screen shows what is set.
  • Adds separate SMS and WhatsApp opt-in checkboxes at the checkout, off until you turn them on in Senderz.
  • Settings you had already chosen on this site are carried over the first time it connects, so nothing is reset.

2.0.2

  • Keeps WordPress integration lookup separate from optional WooCommerce storefront features so published popups resolve correctly.

2.0.1

  • Prepares the plugin for WordPress.org directory submission and confirms compatibility with WordPress 7.0.

2.0.0

  • Replaces Senderz for WooCommerce with one plugin for any WordPress site.
  • Captures submissions from Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor Pro
    Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms and Ninja Forms, with a per-form field
    mapping screen and per-form marketing consent that defaults to off.
  • Adds a guided connect flow, so credentials no longer have to be pasted by hand.
  • WooCommerce checkout opt-in and order recovery links now load only when
    WooCommerce is active.
  • Adds WooCommerce cart and checkout activity for identified shoppers, and an
    optional back-in-stock request form on out-of-stock products, both under
    Senderz Marketing, then Store.
  • All outbound behaviour is gated on the connection.
